data.mechanism: Insulin binds the insulin receptor, which phosphorylates IRS proteins; those recruit PI3K, which makes PIP3 and so starts the arm that reaches mTORC1 through Akt. The step is also where the pathway's best-known feedback lands: S6K1 depletes IRS1/2 and the cell goes deaf to insulin (SHA2004).
data.mechanism_beginner: Insulin lands on its own receptor on the cell surface. The message is passed inward by IRS proteins to PI3K, which builds a signalling lipid, and that is the beginning of the route to mTORC1. This is also the step that breaks when the pathway is overactive for too long.
data.boundary: Insulin and IGF-1 share this receptor arm; growth hormone does not, and is kept separate for that reason. The amplitude and the time pattern of the insulin signal are not interchangeable: KUB2012 shows the AKT pathway multiplexes insulin's temporal pattern, so a single arrow understates what the cell reads. Cell and genetic work, plus human physiology for the insulin-resistance end of it.
